bull_bear.body:
- Integrated service portfolio spanning IT Infrastructure Solutions, Cloud Enablement, Enterprise Security, Banking Solutions and Product Engineering & Development, positioning it as a one-stop enterprise digital transformation partner
- Global parentage and domain expertise supporting presence across India and select international markets
- Diversified presence across key industries -- BFSI, telecommunications, manufacturing, healthcare and the public sector -- broadening addressable demand
- High process-maturity accreditations (CMMI Level 5, multiple ISO certifications, SOC 2 Type II alignment) support enterprise and BFSI client trust
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Global macroeconomic and geopolitical uncertainty — Elevated interest rates, persistent inflation, geopolitical conflicts (including the US-Iran conflict in the Middle East) and trade disruptions create a cautious global business environment that can constrain discretionary enterprise IT spending and elongate deal cycles.
- US economic slowdown / recession risk — S&P Global-cited probability of a US recession over the next 12 months has increased, which could dampen technology investment cycles, including AI-led capex, among US clients.
- US trade policy and H-1B visa tightening — Evolving US trade/tariff policy and tighter immigration norms around H-1B visas introduce greater uncertainty for export-oriented sectors including IT services, moderating growth and elongating deal cycles.
- Indian election-cycle related investment deferral — Upcoming major state elections and by-elections across multiple constituencies may create a restrained investment environment, with investors deferring large capital commitments and causing a temporary slowdown in private investment and increased financial-market volatility.

business.title: Competitive strengths

outlook.body:
- Growth strategy anchored in modernization, with a focus on building scalable, secure and agile solutions aligned to enterprise needs
- Aligning service portfolio with enterprise priorities and emphasizing outcome-driven delivery
- Continuing to strengthen capabilities across core service lines -- infrastructure services, banking technology solutions, product engineering and emerging technology-led offerings
- Talent acquisition and retention treated as a critical competitive advantage, with continued investment in training and capability building
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body:
- India remains a core growth market for Inspirisys, particularly across infrastructure modernisation, banking transformation and enterprise digital adoption
- Revenue growth was primarily driven by the Infra Products and Banking segments within the Indian market
- Domestic market growth was slowed in FY26 by global uncertainties, including the ongoing Russia-Ukraine conflict, which delayed project closures, particularly in the PSU/Government and Banking-focused Infra Products business
- The US market remained subdued during FY26, with management anticipating a recovery in FY27
- Enterprise IT spending is expected to stay selective, with discretionary spend constrained but investments in infrastructure modernisation, cybersecurity, cloud optimisation and AI-led efficiency expected to sustain
- Customer expectations around cost efficiency, measurable outcomes and faster execution are likely to influence deal cycles and pricing dynamics
